conviction_note: The evidence points mostly toward a guided, in-line quarter. Small offsetting items (marketing coming down, FY guide above Street, a crowded short against a planned provision build, Upstart's macro warning, a 35-vol-point put skew) net to impact_sum +1.1. The scaled number is p_up 52 x abs_move 20 = +0.8. The move is expected to be large on the first FY2027 guide, which this print probably carries (the Nov-2025 Q3 print gave the first FY2026 guide), but its sign is not knowable from public sources.
bar: Company FY2026 guide (primary, Q2 release 2026-08-06): revenue growth ~35% (~$607.9M), adj. net income $185M, adj. EPS $5.25; H2 revenue growth ~30%; provision 2.5-3.0% of GMV; revenue yield normalising to ~11.4%. https://finviz.com/news/378863/sezzle-reports-second-quarter-2026-results and https://www.tikr.com/blog/sezzle-stock-plunges-cautious-h2-outlook-earnings-beat . Q3 consensus adj. EPS $1.28 / revenue ~$154.0M (+32% y/y) comes from ONE source (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-27, https://finviz.com/news/409647/sezzles-third-guidance-raise-faces-a-credit-and-marketing-test-in-the-third-quarter). A TD Cowen Q3 EPS estimate of $1.31 (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/sezzle-aktie-steigt-nach-upgrade-td-cowen-stuft-von-hold-auf-buy, 2026-08-10) roughly agrees. FY consensus is $5.10 / $592.6M, below the guide (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/SEZL). Q3 bar not confirmed by two independent sources, so Q3-line findings are capped small. Guide-implied Q3 revenue is ~$152M (Q3-25 $116.8M x 1.30).
positioning_check: Short interest 4,430,122 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 4,221,778 on 2026-09-30; 13.2% of 33.68M shares outstanding; days to cover 9.23 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sezl/shortinterest). CEO Youakim alone reports 13.41M shares (39.6%) in a Schedule 13D/A of 2026-09-14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1662991/000166299126000155/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X01/primary_doc.xml), so free float is at most ~20M and short is at least ~22% of float; Benzinga shows 24.2% of float (undated). Crowded and building into the print. Options: 25d skew +34.97 vol points (puts much richer), put/call OI 1.09, event-implied move 15.95%, ATM IV 120%. Tape: +21.8% over 20d, +6.7% over 5d, still -26% from the 52w high. So the option market has paid for downside while shorts are crowded, and the two cut against each other.

findings.finding: Company FY2026 guide (adj. EPS $5.25, revenue ~$607.9M, adj. NI $185M, raised three times this year) sits above the Street's FY consensus of $5.10 / $592.6M. A reaffirm with an in-line Q3 is therefore a beat against FY consensus, and the company has raised at every 2026 print (Feb, May, Aug).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raises were bought +35.3% (2026-02-25) and +16.0% (2026-05-06). The Aug 2026 raise to $5.25 was sold -33.9% because H2 growth was guided to ~30% (baseline moves; https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/sezl-stock-eyes-worst-day-in-a-year-on-mixed-analyst-actions-cautious-h2-guidance/cZofiXgRJ9u).
findings.why_not_priced: If the Street believed the guide, FY consensus would sit at or above $5.25. It sits at $5.10, so analysts are discounting the guide after the August H2-deceleration sell-off. The 35-point put skew says the market leans to disappointment, not to a fourth raise.
findings.independence: Guide history table is from the company's Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/378863/sezzle-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). The FY consensus figures appear in both Earnings Whispers and the finviz-hosted preview, which are likely the same origin, so count them as one source.

findings.finding: Q2 marketing, advertising and tradeshow spend was $19.4M (vs $8.8M in 2Q25), and management said it was not a run rate and would come down in Q3. Q3 operating leverage therefore has a stated tailwind, and consensus Q3 EPS of $1.28 is up from Q2's actual $1.13.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, record marketing-driven subscriber adds (+140k) came with an EPS beat ($1.13 vs $0.95-1.03), and the stock still fell 33.9% on the forward guide. This line has not decided a reaction on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management said it on the August call, and the Q3 EPS consensus step-up reflects it. It stays a finding because elevated spend would read as an acquisition-efficiency problem, so the line is two-sided. It lands inside what the company guided.
findings.independence: TIKR's Q2 recap also reports a planned Q3 marketing scale-back (https://www.tikr.com/blog/sezzle-stock-plunges-cautious-h2-outlook-earnings-beat). Q2 marketing dollars come from the company release (https://finviz.com/news/378863/sezzle-reports-second-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: Credit build is guided: Q2 provision was 2.4% of GMV ($30.6M) against an FY framework of 2.5-3.0%, so H2 provisions must rise and a single quarter could top 3%. The record 140k Q2 subscriber cohort is maturing, and SezzleCash (cash advance) had its first full quarter in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026, credit trends better than expected were cited for the beat, and the stock rose 16.0% on 2026-05-06. No print in the window was sold on credit.
findings.why_not_priced: The rise in provisions is guided, so a provision near 3% of GMV is inside the framework and largely priced. The unpriced risk is a figure above 3%, or net transaction margin falling well below Q2's 63.5%. Nothing public on Q3 Sezzle credit exists between prints. A crowded short (22%+ of float) shrinks this negative.
findings.independence: The finviz preview flags the same >3% risk (https://finviz.com/news/409647/sezzles-third-guidance-raise-faces-a-credit-and-marketing-test-in-the-third-quarter). Both trace back to management's own framework, so this is one fact.

findings.finding: This print probably carries the first FY2027 outlook. At the Q3 2025 print (2025-11-05) Sezzle gave its first FY2026 EPS guide ($4.35), and the stock fell 12.5% that session. The forward guide is where this name's reaction lives, and growth was already guided to slow from ~40% in H1 to ~30% in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-guide print 2025-11-05: -12.5%. Raised-guide prints: +35.3% (Feb 2026), +16.0% (May 2026), -33.9% (Aug 2026, on H2 deceleration). Forward growth is the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody knows the number. No FY2027 consensus was found in any public source, so whatever is guided is new information. The sign is unknown. The small negative reflects last year's first-guide reaction and the guided deceleration path. The 35-point put skew is consistent with the market fearing exactly this.
findings.independence: The guide history table (Nov 2025 column $4.35 EPS) is in the company's Q2 2026 release. The 2025-11-05 move is from the sealed baseline. Both rest on company documents.

findings.finding: Upstart (consumer-credit peer, reported 2026-11-03 before this print): CEO said 'Macro is putting pressure on our near-term outlook'. Its FY2026 guide of ~$1.35B total revenue implies Q4 revenue of roughly $307M against Q3's $371M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No documented SEZL reaction to an Upstart print was found.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed one session before the print, after Sezzle last spoke in August, and the stock still rose into the print (+6.7% over 5d), so the read-across may be under-weighted. It is a proxy: Upstart is unsecured personal loans funded by capital markets, not BNPL subscriptions, and Sezzle has not confirmed any macro pressure. A crowded short shrinks this negative.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Q4 implied figure is derived arithmetic from Upstart's FY guide. Klarna separately said late-Q2 softness continued into Q3 (see the Klarna finding), which is a different source.

findings.finding: PayPal's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-27): Pay Later volume grew 25% y/y, and PayPal raised FY non-GAAP guidance. That is a direct BNPL demand read for the same quarter, with no sign of a Q3 consumer pullback in US pay-later.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No documented SEZL reaction to a PayPal print was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: SEZL rose from ~$126.5 (Oct 26) to $138.7 into the print. It is a proxy, because PayPal's pay-later is a larger, prime-skewed book. The +25% figure comes from a secondary summary of the call (https://moneycheck.com/paypal-pypl-processes-487-1-billion-in-payments-while-repurchasing-1-5-billion-in-shares/), not from the release itself.
findings.independence: Affirm's guide for its Sept quarter (GMV $13.7-14.0B, revenue above Street; https://finviz.com/news/398879/affirm-to-announce-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-results-on-november-5-2026) points the same way but was issued in August and is guidance, not an actual.

findings.finding: Crowded and building short into the print: 4.43M shares short at 2026-10-15 (+4.9% vs 2026-09-30), at least ~22% of float with the founder's 39.6% stake excluded, 9.2 days to cover. Event-implied move is 15.95% against a 35-vol-point put skew.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Recent upside surprises on this name ran +35.3% and +16.0%, consistent with short covering amplifying good prints. Downside prints ran -33.9% and -12.5%, so the squeeze does not stop the stock falling on a bad guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew is pricing the downside. If shorts expected a clean print they would be covering, but the position grew into October. Any in-line-plus-reaffirm outcome forces covering against 9 days of volume. This is positioning, not fundamentals, and it is sized small because the option market is on the other side.
findings.independence: Benzinga shows 24.2% of float short (undated; https://jp.benzinga.com/quote/SEZL/sentiment). The float arithmetic uses the CEO's 13D/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1662991/000166299126000155/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X01/primary_doc.xml).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue bar sits slightly above the company's own H2 path. Consensus ~$154.0M (+32%) compares with ~$151.8M implied by ~30% H2 growth, and management guided revenue yield down sequentially as Pagaya referrals and SezzleCash dilute take rate (Q2 total revenue/GMV 11.7%, FY ~11.4%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sezzle beat revenue consensus by ~10% in Q2 ($149.7M vs ~$135-136M) and still fell 33.9%. Revenue beats have not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: The yield dilution was guided, so it is inside guidance. The gap between consensus and the guide-implied path is ~1.5%, well inside Sezzle's recent beat sizes. This is a capped, single-source bar item.
findings.independence: Yield normalisation to ~11.4% is in the Q2 recap (https://www.tikr.com/blog/sezzle-stock-plunges-cautious-h2-outlook-earnings-beat). The Pagaya program is from Pagaya's 2026-05-05 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260505549218/en/Pagaya-Announces-New-Point-of-Sale-Partnership-With-Sezzle-to-Expand-Consumers-Options-for-Sezzle-Customers).

findings.finding: WebBank program amended and restated on 2026-08-12 (8-K filed 2026-08-18). It adds SezzleCash and Sezzle Send, with WebBank retaining those loans (retention threshold $30M, expandable to $150M), raises Sezzle's minimum tangible net worth covenant from $12M to $100M, and adds termination events. Economics on existing products are unchanged and the term runs to 2029-09-27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reaction to the filing is identifiable; it landed in the post-Q2 drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: On what the money buys: the amendment funds the two new products off Sezzle's balance sheet, which supports a product ramp, not distress. The $100M net-worth floor is well below a company earning $185M adjusted a year. The full agreements will be exhibits to the Q3 10-Q, so terms may get attention on the call. Small positive.
findings.independence: SezzleCash uptake (~$165 average advance, ~10% of eligible new subscribers using it first) is reported in Q2 call coverage (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/sezzle-send-launch-can-p2p-virality-drive-low-cost-growth, fetch failed; snippet only).

findings.finding: Management's FY2026 guide assumes zero from Sezzle Send (P2P, slated for August launch, >100k waitlist) and little from SezzleCash. Any Q3 contribution or launch metrics are upside to the guide, and no post-launch figure is public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: New-product commentary (SezzleCash in Q2) came with record subscriber adds, but the print was sold on H2 deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: No public data exists on whether Send launched or how it performed, so nothing can be priced. It is small next to the core BNPL/subscription book (854k subscribers), which has to hold for this to matter.
findings.independence: Q2 call coverage repeats the zero-in-guide assumption (search snippet of https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/sezzle-send-launch-can-p2p-virality-drive-low-cost-growth). Launch is unverified.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Sezzle filed with the OCC for a national bank charter (Sezzle Bank, N.A.) plus FDIC deposit insurance, pivoting from its Utah ILC plan, with approval expected in 12-18 months. The call will likely cover charter costs and capital plans, which could enter the FY2027 framework.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean reaction identifiable. The stock was ~$126-130 in late October.
findings.why_not_priced: The application is public. What is not priced is the cost and capital the bank build needs, and whether it shows up in FY2027 opex. Two-sided, near zero.

findings.finding: Klarna (2026-08-18) said softness that emerged late in Q2 continued into Q3 and cut its FY GMV outlook to $149-151B from >$155B, mostly on Germany. US GMV grew +27% in Q2 and provisions were 0.52% of GMV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No documented SEZL reaction to Klarna prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is two months old and overlapped Sezzle's own August sell-off. Klarna's softness is European, and its US leg grew, so transmission to Sezzle's US-only book is weak.
findings.independence: The Q3-continuation comment is from search summary of Klarna Q2 coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/klarna-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-18/). PayPal's Q3 Pay Later +25% points the other way for the US.

outside_window.finding: Affirm reports its Sept-quarter (FQ1 2027) after the close on 2026-11-05, after this window ends, so it can re-rate the BNPL group only after the trade exits.
Klarna Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-17, a direct BNPL peer read that lands after the window.
FINRA short interest for the 2026-10-30 settlement is published 2026-11-10 (Equibles model estimate 4.59M shares).
Annual meeting 2026-11-19 (virtual). Investor conferences 2026-11-09 to 12-09 (BMO, Citi, KBW, TD Cowen, Needham).

searched_and_found_nothing: 8-K item 2.02 of 2026-10-08 (the +9.74% baseline 'reaction'): only the Q3 date/conference announcement, no preliminary numbers. Sezzle does not pre-release between prints. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1662991/000166299126000165/sezl-20261008ex9901.htm
8-K of 2026-08-28 (Item 8.01): annual-meeting logistics only, no buyback or dividend
Management commentary at the Sept 15/17 2026 conferences (Oppenheimer, FT Partners, BTIG): no coverage found
App download / review / card-panel data for Sezzle in Q3 2026: no public series found
Q3 2026 BNPL delinquency survey data: only 2025/early-2026 surveys, not company-level
Sezzle Send post-launch metrics: no source confirms launch

Insider Form 4/144 in Sept-Oct 2026: two Form 144s on 2026-10-09 and Form 4s in Sept exist, but no coverage gives the amounts. The 13D/A of 2026-09-14 shows no open-market sale (a divorce-related trust removal)
Regulatory action on SezzleCash or CFPB: none found. Only May-2026 plaintiff-firm investigation notices
FY2027 consensus: not found in any public source

rejected_candidates.detail: The 2026-10-08, 2026-07-14 and probably 2026-04-15 and 2026-02-02 rows are date-announcement 8-Ks (10-08 exhibit confirmed). The rebuilt base rate on the four true prints (-12.5, +35.3, +16.0, -33.9) has a median |move| of ~25%.

rejected_candidates.detail: Seven months old, and three prints and the May plaintiff-firm notices have since absorbed it. It does not bear on this quarter beyond the governance overhang already in the positioning finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Wire copy. It carries no information beyond the bar already stated.

baseline_tension: What I found mostly agrees with what the market has priced: a guided quarter with a decisive forward guide. The one cut against the 35-point put skew and the +21.8% run-up is the crowded, rising short and the Street sitting below the company's FY guide. That is why p_up sits at 52 rather than below 50, and the skew is why it is not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold the Aug beat-and-raise -33.9%): FY-guide-above-consensus finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8.

Lesson 7 (sign against a strong 35-point put skew): positioning/squeeze finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6. Crowded short (22%+ of float, 9.2 DTC) shrinks the negatives: provision build -0.7 to -0.5, Upstart macro proxy -0.6 to -0.4.
Lesson 6 (bar): Q3 consensus has one source, so Q3-line findings stay capped small and print_vs_bar cut from +4 to +3. The FY bar is sourced to the company guide.
Rebuilt base rate from confirmed releases (lesson on untrustworthy history): four true prints, median ~25% against 15.95% implied. abs_move raised from 19 to 20. p_up unchanged at 52.
Left standing: first-FY2027-guide finding (-0.5, wide range), PayPal/Klarna proxies, WebBank financing (signed after asking what it funds), Send, and bank charter.
